title: Name the actual review channel and do not invent a session identity
problem: A record saying that HORUS reviewed work can be mistaken for a separate named ChatGPT conversation or an external peer review.
failure: The earlier phrase “reviewed in-session” was ambiguous. For the cited work, the reviewer was an internal analytical collaboration agent; no separate ChatGPT conversation or provider-issued session ID existed.
correction: Describe the actual participant and execution channel explicitly: internal analytical agent review; no standalone conversation/session ID; model-side review, not human peer review.
transfer: Before claiming a named chair session, external review, or independent peer review, identify the actual runtime participant and recover its genuine session identifier. If none exists, say so.
limits: This card records the specific R18/PR29 provenance correction and internal review. It does not establish a general review protocol or make internal model analysis equivalent to human peer review.
